'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**Two more [[State of Palestine|Palestinian]] protestors, aged 18 and 20, die from wounds sustained in clashes at the [[Israeli–Gazan border]]. Both were shot by [[Israeli Defence Forces|Israeli troops]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2018-04-23/2-palestinians-die-of-wounds-sustained-in-gaza-protests (US News)]
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**A [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led coalition airstrike kills [[Yemen]]'s [[Supreme Political Council]] president [[Saleh Ali al-Sammad]]. He was considered the most senior [[Houthis|Houthi]] official in [[Sana'a]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-43872482 (BBC)]
**[[2018 Hajjah Governorate airstrike|An airstrike]] hits a wedding procession in [[Bani Qa'is District]] in [[Yemen]]'s northwestern [[Hajjah Governorate]], killing between 22 and 33 people, according to Yemeni health officials. [http://www.scmp.com/news/world/middle-east/article/2142967/saudi-attack-yemen-wedding-kills-least-20-wounds-dozens (''South China Morning Post'')] 
*[[2018 Toronto van attack]]
**A van strikes a group of pedestrians in [[Toronto]], [[Canada]], killing ten and injuring sixteen. According to the [[Toronto Police Service]], the driver, who fled the scene, was later arrested. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43873804 (BBC)] [https://globalnews.ca/news/4161785/pedestrians-hit-white-van-toronto/ (Globe News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/23/toronto-van-crash-incident-latest-updates-canada (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-43875321 (BBC)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Freedom of speech in Egypt]]
**[[United Nations]] cultural authority [[UNESCO]] awards imprisoned [[Egypt]]ian photojournalist [[Mahmoud Abu Zeid]] the [[UNESCO/Guillermo Cano World Press Freedom Prize|2018 Guillermo Cano World Press Freedom Prize]], drawing criticism from Egypt. Abu Zeid faces the [[capital punishment|death penalty]]. [http://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/jailed-egyptian-photojournalist-to-be-awarded-2018-press-freedom-prize (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Israel]]i lawmakers [[Yuval Steinitz]] and [[Oren Hazan]] accuse [[Jerusalem]]-born actress [[Natalie Portman]] of [[antisemitism]] and seek to revoke her citizenship with Hazan calling her a "little hyprocrite liar" after she decides not to travel to Israel and accept the [[US$]]2 million [[Genesis Prize]]. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/173012-180423-oren-hazan-will-push-to-revoke-natalie-portman-s-citizenship (i24 News)]
*[[Beverley Folk Festival]] in [[England]] collapses into administration. [http://www.nme.com/news/music/beverley-folk-festival-goes-administration-no-refunds-available-2300463 (NME)]
*[[Catherine, Duchess of Cambridge]] gives birth to her and the [[William, Duke of Cambridge|Duke]]'s third child and second boy; the child is fifth in line to the [[Monarchy of the United Kingdom|British throne]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-43864933 (BBC)]

'''Business and economy'''
*Underwater engineering firm [[Subsea 7]] begins negotiations to acquire offshore company [[McDermott International]], offering [[US$]]2 billion for it. [https://splash247.com/subsea-7-moves-acquire-mcdermott-2bn-wants-cbi-deal-scrapped/ (''Splash 24/7'')]
*The [[Finland|Finnish]] [[Politics of Finland|government]] decides not to expand a small two-year trial of [[universal basic income]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43866700 (BBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2018]]
**Ferry operator [[DFDS]] has discontinued their [[Rosyth – Zeebrugge ferry service]]. DFDS says it is no longer profitable to operate the route. The change follows a fire aboard the MV ''Finlandia Seaways'' a day before. The [[Scottish government]] seeks urgent talks between DFDS and Transport Secretary [[Humza Yousaf]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-edinburgh-east-fife-43864813 (BBC)]
*[[2018 North Korea bus accident]]
**A bus crash in [[North Hwanghae]], [[North Korea]], kills 32 [[China|Chinese]] tourists and four North Koreans. A further two people are seriously injured. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/north-korea-bus-crash-latest-updates-china-killed-tourists-traffic-accident-a8317636.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Southwest Airlines Flight 1380]]
**[[Southwest Airlines]] cancels 128 flights in addition to 40 cancelled yesterday as it inspects the [[CFM56-7B]] engines mounted to its [[Boeing 737]] fleet following a fatal accident. [https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/airplane-mode/southwest-cancels-dozens-flights-engine-inspections-wake-deadly-midair-explosion-n868371 (NBC News)]
*[[2010 Polish Air Force Tu-154 crash]]
**[[European Commission]] President [[Donald Tusk]] testifies in [[Warsaw]] about the disaster which killed 96 including then-[[President of Poland|President]] [[Lech Kaczynski]]. Tusk was [[Prime Minister of Poland|Prime Minister]] at the time. He is locked in disputes with [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] over the crash. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/donald-tusk-poland-president-plane-crash-2010-warsaw-court-russia-a8318316.html (The Independent)]

'''Health and environment'''
*Doctors at the [[Johns Hopkins University]] in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]], perform the world's first successful transplant of a [[penis]] and [[scrotum]] from a deceased donor to a U.S. soldier injured in [[Afghanistan]]. The [[testicles]] are not transplanted. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43873058 (BBC)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea]] ceases loudspeaker broadcasts directed at soldiers over the [[North Korea]]n border ahead of a [[April 2018 inter-Korean summit|planned meeting]] later this week between leaders [[Moon Jae-in]] and [[Kim Jong Un]]. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/asia-pacific/172954-180423-s-korea-halts-border-broadcasts-ahead-of-kim-summit (i24 News)]
*[[Nicaragua–United States relations]]
**The [[U.S. State Department]] orders the families of U.S. diplomats in [[Nicaragua]] to leave amid riots by protestors against proposed pension changes. President [[Daniel Ortega]] has scrapped the changes but further protests are nonetheless anticipated. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-43860848 (BBC)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Bosnian War]]
**[[Radovan Karadžić]] starts his appeal against his conviction for [[genocide]] and other wartime crimes at the UN court at [[The Hague]]. [http://www.balkaninsight.com/en/article/radovan-karadzic-appeals-unjust-genocide-conviction-04-20-2018 (''Balkan Transitional Justice'')]
*[[Freedom of speech in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Scotland|Scottish]] [[YouTube]]r [[Mark Meechan|Mark "Count Dankula" Meechan]] is fined [[Pound sterling|£]]800 for a [[hate crime|racially aggravated]] offence under the [[Communications Act 2003|Communications Act]] for a video of a pug dog responding to [[Nazi]] slogans. Protests are held outside [[Airdrie, North Lanarkshire|Airdrie]] [[Sheriff Court]] and [[English Defence League]] ex-leader [[Tommy Robinson (activist)|Tommy Robinson]] sits in court to support Meechan. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-43864133 (BBC)]
*[[Murder of Stephen Lawrence]]
**[[UK]] [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]] announces that henceforth April 22 will be marked nationally as Stephen Lawrence Day to commemorate the black teenager murdered 25 years ago in a [[hate crime|racist assault]]. The high-profile crime led to the [[Metropolitan Police]] being [[Macpherson report|labeled]] "institutionally racist". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-43869377 (BBC)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/04/22/police-still-institutionally-racist-25-years-stephen-lawrence/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Death of Kim Wall]]
**[[Denmark|Danish]] prosecutors seek a life sentence for [[Peter Madsen]], accused of murdering a [[Sweden|Swedish]] journalist on board his self-built submarine. [[Psychiatry|Psychiatric]] evidence describes Madsen as presenting "psychopathic traits" and a "high risk" of offending further. [http://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/perverse-polymorph-with-psychopathic-traits-life-term-sought-for-danish-submariner-over (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Nashville Waffle House shooting]]
**Travis Reinking, suspected of shooting and killing four people in a [[Waffle House]] restaurant in [[Antioch, Tennessee]], is captured following a police manhunt. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/news/waffle-house-suspect-still-being-sought-residents-alert-051218724.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[Piracy in the 21st century]]
**The owners of the [[Netherlands|Dutch]] ship MV ''FWN Rapide'' announce the ship was attacked by [[piracy|pirates]] last night while sailing from [[Ghana]] to [[Nigeria]] and 12 of the crew abducted. [https://splash247.com/dutch-ship-attacked-nigeria-hostages-taken/ (''Splash 24/7'')]
*[[November 2015 Paris attacks]]
**Suspect [[Salah Abdeslam]] and a co-defendant are convicted of attempting to murder police officers and terror offences in [[Belgium]], with each receiving a 20-year sentence. Abdeslam is being held in [[France]] awaiting trial for the 2015 attacks. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43862873 (BBC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2018 Armenian protests]]
**[[Serzh Sargsyan]] resigns as [[Armenia]]'s prime minister after eleven days of large street protests against him. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/23/serzh-sargsyan-resigns-as-armenias-prime-minister-after-protests (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Reza Shah's mausoleum|Mausoleum of Reza Shah]]
**A mummified body is found at [[Shahr-e Rey]] which [[Iran]]ian media reports possibly belongs to former country's king, [[Reza Shah]]. His [[Reza Shah's mausoleum|mausoleum]] was destroyed after [[1979 Revolution]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/mideast/2018/04/23/iranian-officials-discover-body-of-reza-shah-pahlavi (''The Daily Sabah'')]
*[[Politics of Malawi]]
**Former [[Malawi]]an [[President of Malawi|President]] [[Joyce Banda]] announces she is to return from three years of exile amid a corruption scandal. [http://www.euronews.com/2018/04/23/former-malawi-president-joyce-banda-returns-from-exile (Euronews)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**A study reveals that [[WASP-104b]], a [[hot Jupiter]] [[exoplanet]], is darker than [[charcoal]] and absorbs 99% of light. [https://www.inquisitr.com/4875067/darker-than-coal-researchers-find-a-hot-jupiter-that-absorbs-nearly-99-percent-of-light/ (''The Inquisitr'')] [https://www.i4u.com/2018/04/127987/hot-jupiter-wasp-104b-darker-charcoal (I4U)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2018 London Marathon]]
**It is confirmed runner Matt Campbell, a former ''[[MasterChef: The Professionals|MasterChef]]'' semifinalist, died in hospital after collapsing during yesterday's [[London Marathon]]. The race was the hottest since the annual event began. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cumbria-43864835 (BBC)]
